full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana, J. The State has filed all these 3 Criminal Petitions for Leave to Appeal against the judgment an order dated 08.04.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Death Reference No. 49 of 2006 heard along with Criminal Appeal No. 2409 of 2006, 2410 of 2006, 2417 of 2006, Jail Appeal No. 366 of 2006 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 8191 of 2006 rejecting the death reference and also dismissing the Criminal Appeal No. 2409 of 2006 and Jail Appeal No. 366 of 2006 confirming the conviction of the accused appellant Apel but commuting his sentence of death to imprisonment for life and allowing the other appeals and thereby acquitting all the other convicted accused persons. 

 2. The case of the prosecution, in short, was that on 25.04.2004 accused Appel, Jewel, Rubel and Sagar accompanied by other 5/6 terrorists under the leadership of accused Apel came to the shop of informant's younger sister's caretaker Mojibar and demanded tolls from the said caretaker. They beat caretaker Mojibar and his brother Sultan and snatched away cash money, sewing machine etc. on their refusal to pay tolls. On the same day, in the evening, they set fire to the house of caretaker Mojibar. That the accused persons were associated with extraction of tolls and various types of criminal activities and the informant and his other family members raised their voice against the accused persons and at this the accused persons held out threats openly to kill the informant and his family members. Thereafter, on 28.04.2004 at about 12.20 P.M. the accused persons, namely, Ismail Hossain Mollah, Apel, Ilius, Jewel alias Shakhawat Hossain Molla, Hero, Rubel alias Md. Sahadat Hossain Molla, Zillur Rahman alias Masum, Momen, Azad, Humayoon, Sagar and Noor Nabi, being armed with sharp cutting weapons and fire arms, all on a sudden attacked informant's brother Hashem (deceased) and started inflicting blows, kicks and stabs on him. Hashem fell down on the ground receiving those blows, kicks and stabs and at that stage the accused Ilius, Jewel, Hero, Rubel and Zillur Rahman caught hold of the deceased and accused Apel dealt blows with a sharp cutting knife on the left thigh and lower abdomen causing grievous injuries. The accused persons thereafter left the place of occurrence. The neighboring persons then took Hashem to Hospital where he succumbed to his injuries. 

 3. The informant Kazi Mahmud Hasan, Brigadier General (Retired), after hearing the occurrence from the witnesses lodged F.I.R. with Joydevpur P.S. on the same day. On the basis of that F.I.R. Joydevpur P.S. Case No. 63(4) 2004 under Sections 302/34/109 of the Penal Code was started. The Police, after completion of investigation submitted charge sheet against the accused persons under sections 302/34/209 of the Penal Code. The case was thereafter transferred to the Court of Sessions Judge, Gazipur. But subsequently the case was transferred to the Druto Bichar Tribunal No. 3, Dhaka and was numbered as Druto Bicar Tribunal Case No. 15 of 2005. This tribunal held trial after framing formal charge under sections 302/34/109 of the Penal Code against the accused Ismail Hossan Molla and under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code against the rest 11 accused persons. The charge so framed were read over and explained to the accused persons who faced trial. 

 4. The prosecution examined 18 witnesses. The accused persons, who were present in dock, were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The defence case was a plea of innocence. The learned Judge of the Druto Beichar tribunal considering the evidence adduced by the prosecution, found the accused Apel guilty of the charge under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and convicted and sentenced him thereunder to death. The tribunal convicted the accused Ilius, Jewel alias Shakhawat Hossain Molla, Hero, Rubel alias Md. Sahadat Hossain Molla, Zillur Rahman alias Masum, Momen, Azad, Humayoon and Sagar also under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced them thereunder to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay fine of Tk. 50,000/- each. The tribunal acquitted accused Ismail Hossain Molla and accused Noor Nabi finding them not guilty of the charge framed against them. 

 5. On a reference made by the trial court for confirmation of death sentence of accused Apel the above mentioned Death Reference No. 49 of 2006 was started. Condemned-prisoner Apel preferred Criminal Appeal No. 2409 of 2006 and also Jail Appeal No. 366 of 2006 against his conviction and sentence. The other convicted accused persons also filed other criminal appeals and criminal miscellaneous case as mentioned above. A Division Bench of the High Court Division heard the death reference and all the criminal appeals, Jail appeals and the criminal miscellaneous case together and by the impugned judgment and order disposed of all those as already mentioned above. The High Court Division found that the prosecution could prove the charge against the accused Apel only and as such affirmed his conviction, but considering his tender age and other facts and circumstances commuted the death sentence imposed on him by the trial court to a sentence of imprisonment for life with fine. The High court Division found that the prosecution could not prove the charges against the other accused persons by adducing cogent evidence and as such acquitted all the other convicted accused persons by the impugned Judgment and order. 

 7. Mr. Khondaker Diliruzzaman, the learned Deputy Attorney General has assailed the impugned judgment of the High Court Division making submission to the effect that the High Court Division was not justified at all to commute the death sentence of accused Apel to imprisonment for life and also acquit the other convicted accused-respondents. The learned Deputy Attorney General has argued that considering the brutality of the allegation the trial court rightly sentenced the accused Apel to death, but the High Court Division most unjustly has commuted the sentence of Death to imprisonment for life. As regards the other accused-respondents, the learned Deputy Attorney General has made argument to the effect that there are sufficient evidence to prove the charge against these accused-respondents and the trial court, on consideration of these evidence, rightly convicted and sentenced these accused-respondents, but the High Court Division, without appreciation these evidence, most whimsically and arbitrarily acquitted the other accused persons causing miscarriage of justice. The learned Deputy Attorney General has argued that the evidence which the prosecution has adduced in this case are sufficient to prove the charges against the other accused persons also beyond all reasonable doubt and in the circumstances the High Court Division committed illegality in acquitting these accused persons.
